title: Diagnostic: some View Must Be One Type
hints: An opaque return type must be the same concrete type on every path.
Return `Text` on one path and `Image` on the other with explicit `return`s.
jsBridge: `some View` must be **one** concrete type, so returning `Text` in one branch and `Image` in another fails. `@ViewBuilder` wraps branches into `_ConditionalContent`. JSX never has this issue because elements share one runtime type.

compass.q: A React function can return `<Text/>` or `<Image/>` freely. Why can't a Swift `some View` function?
Fixes: `@ViewBuilder`, `Group { if … }`, or `AnyView`. Which is cheapest?
Why does `body` not need `@ViewBuilder` written explicitly? (The `View` protocol declares it.)
Helper functions returning views: do you mark them `@ViewBuilder` by habit?
